title_ar: الشيخ الددو يستنكر القتل والتهجير الذي حل بالشعب السوري الأعزل ويدعو لنصرته
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Condemns the Killing and Displacement that has Befallen the Defenceless Syrian People and Calls for Support for Them
body_ar:
في خطبته للجمعة أمس بجامع أسامة بعرفات دعا الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء إلى نصرة الشعب السوري والوقوف معه في ثورته ضد الظلم والاستبداد، قائلا: " إننا في هذه الأيام نشهد في أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يحصل في كثير من المناطق من ظلم الأقوياء للضعفاء وهو أمر لا يمكن أن يُتحمل؛ شاهدنا ظلم الأجانب وتنكيلهم بالمسلمين وغزوهم لبلادهم والعبث بمقدساتهم فكان ذلك أمرا معقولا لأن يقع من أعداء الله أن يتسلطوا على أولياء الله، لكن الذي هو أنكى من ذلك وأوجع أن يعتدي من يدعي الإسلام من المسلمين من الذين ملكهم الله رقاب شعوبهم أن يعتدوا على شعوبهم المسكينة المضطهدة الفقيرة ويتمادون في ذلك بطغيانهم وبغيهم ولا يرتدعون من أي رادع، ثم بعد ذلك يسكت العالم عنهم كأن شيئا ما وقع".
• وتناول الشيخ في خطبته ما تعيشه الشعوب الإسلامية من حراك وثورة ضد الأنظمة القمعية الفاسدة في اليمن وسوريا وليبيا، مؤكدا على ضرورة نصرتهم في السر والعلن والوقوف معهم في كل المحافل الإعلامية والدولية، وذكَّر أن "العالَم يشهد على ما قام به اليهود من غزو لغزة واحتلالهم لفلسطين وشاهد ما كان من غزو من الأمريكان في أفغانستان والعراق وما شهدته هذه الشعوب من تدنيس لمقدساتها وتدمير لمقدراتها، ثم بعد ذلك جاءت الكارثة من بعض الأنظمة العربية بنفس الأسلوب ونفس الأسلحة ولا يرعون في مسلم إلاَّ ولا ذمة".
• وقال "إن من واجب الأمة أن تنكر المنكر وتأخذ على يد الظالم وتردعه عن الظلم، فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " والذي نفسي بيده لتأمُرُنَّ بالمعروف ولتنهوُنَّ عن المنكر أو ليوشكنَّ الله أن يبعث عليكم عقاباً منه ثم تدعونه فلا يستجاب لكم "، وقال: "لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر ولتأخذن على يد الظالم ولتأطُرُنّه على الحق أطرا". وذكّر الشيخ الحكام العرب الذين وقعوا في هذا المأزق أن ما يقع لهم اليوم من انفلات السلطة من أيديهم إنما هو بسبب كفرهم لنعم الله التي أعطاهم، حيث قال الشيخ – حفظه الله- "إن كثيرا ممن يعطيهم الله القوة في الجسم ويملأ أيديهم من المال ويعطيهم السلطة في الأرض، يغفلون عن نعمة الله فيكفرون بها ولا يقومون لها بحقها ثم يستعينون بها على معصية الله وظلم عباده والبطش في الأرض".
• وأشار الشيخ إلى أن ما نراه اليوم هو من الأحداث التي يكررها التاريخ وهو موعظة لكل الحاكمين وكل من طغى وتجبر في الأرض.. فعلى المؤمن أن يتذكر أخذ الله تبارك وتعالى وعقوبته للماضين ويتذكر عرضه عليه يوم القيامة، وأن يُعد العدة لذلك اليوم العسير.
• ودعا المسلمين إلى أن ترِقّ قلوبهم لرحمة إخوانهم ويدعوا لهم عن ظهر غيب فذلك واجب أمة الجسد الواحد..
• وأكد الشيخ في نهاية الخطبة على ضرورة الوقوف مع الشعب السوري والشعوب الأخرى المنكوبة بالدعاء عن ظهر غيب والتظاهر لنصرته في الإعلام والمحافل العامة، وختم بالدعاء البليغ لعامة المسلمين وخاصتهم من المنكوبين والضعفاء والعُزَّل، ودعا إلى نصرتهم في السر والعلن. محاضرة قيمة حوت مواعظ بليغة، ندعوكم لمتابعتها. اضغط هنا للمتابعة.
body_en:
In his Friday sermon yesterday at the Usamah Mosque in Arafat, Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, called for support for the Syrian people and for standing with them in their revolution against oppression and despotism, saying: "In these days we are witnessing, within the community of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what is occurring in many regions of the oppression of the weak by the strong, and it is a thing that cannot be borne. We have seen the oppression of foreigners, and their brutalising of Muslims, and their invading of their lands, and their tampering with their sanctities; and that was an intelligible thing to occur from the enemies of God, that they should gain mastery over the friends of God. But what is more galling and more painful than that is that those who lay claim to Islam, from among the Muslims whom God has given power over the necks of their own peoples, should assault their wretched, persecuted, impoverished peoples and should persist in that in their tyranny and their transgression, restrained by no restraint; and then, after that, the world falls silent about them as though nothing at all had happened."

• In his sermon the Sheikh treated the ferment and revolution the Muslim peoples are living through against the repressive, corrupt regimes in Yemen, Syria and Libya, affirming the necessity of supporting them in secret and in the open and of standing with them in every media and international forum. He recalled that "the world bears witness to what the Jews have done in invading Gaza, and to their occupation of Palestine, and has seen what invading was done by the Americans in Afghanistan and Iraq, and what these peoples have witnessed of the defiling of their sanctities and the destruction of their resources; and then, after that, the catastrophe came from some of the Arab regimes, by the same method and with the same weapons, observing towards no Muslim either tie of kinship or covenant."

• He said: "It is among the duties of the community that it reject wrong, and take hold of the oppressor's hand, and restrain him from oppression. For the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, you shall enjoin right and you shall forbid wrong, or else God will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will supplicate Him and you will not be answered.' And he said: 'You shall enjoin right, and you shall forbid wrong, and you shall take hold of the oppressor's hand, and you shall bend him to the truth with a firm bending.'" And the Sheikh reminded those Arab rulers who have fallen into this impasse that what is befalling them today, in power slipping from their hands, is on account of their ingratitude for the blessings God gave them — as the Sheikh, may God preserve him, said: "Many of those to whom God gives strength in the body, and whose hands He fills with wealth, and to whom He gives authority in the land, are heedless of God's blessing and so are ungrateful for it and do not fulfil what is due for it, and then call upon it to help them in disobedience to God, and in oppressing His servants, and in violence in the land."

• The Sheikh indicated that what we see today is among the events that history repeats, and is an admonition to all who rule and to everyone who has been tyrannical and overbearing in the land. The believer must call to mind God's seizing, blessed and exalted is He, and His punishment of those who have gone before; and must call to mind his own being presented before Him on the Day of Resurrection; and must make ready provision for that hard day.

• And he called upon the Muslims to let their hearts soften in mercy for their brothers and to supplicate for them in their absence, for that is the duty of a community that is one body.

• At the end of the sermon the Sheikh affirmed the necessity of standing with the Syrian people and the other stricken peoples, by supplicating for them in their absence and by demonstrating in support of them in the media and in public forums. He closed with an eloquent supplication for the Muslims at large and for those of them in particular who are stricken, weak and defenceless, and called for support for them in secret and in the open.

flags.arabic: ما قام به اليهود من غزو لغزة واحتلالهم لفلسطين
flags.context: the Sheikh's sermon, as quoted by the news desk, on the sequence of invasions preceding the Arab uprisings
options: render literally as 'the Jews', as the Arabic has it, and hold for editorial decision
render as 'the Israelis', which the Arabic does not say
render as 'the Jews [i.e. the Israeli forces]' with an inserted gloss
flags.note: CRITICAL — editorial_review. The Arabic word is اليهود, 'the Jews', and the style guide forbids both softening and silent repair, so the English says what the Arabic says. But the choice is consequential: in Arabic political speech of this register the word is routinely used for the Israeli state and its forces, while the English 'the Jews' names a religious and ethnic group, and the sentence as it stands in English attributes the invasion of Gaza and the occupation of Palestine to Jews as such. That is antisemitic in effect whatever was intended, and it carries legal exposure in several jurisdictions in which Ummah Collective may publish. The translator does not resolve this and must not; the decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. Note also that these are the news desk's quotation marks around a paraphrase of spoken words, so even the Arabic wording is not securely the Sheikh's.

flags.arabic: دعا إلى نصرة الشعب السوري والوقوف معه في ثورته ضد الظلم والاستبداد ... الأنظمة القمعية الفاسدة في اليمن وسوريا وليبيا
options: translate faithfully and hold for editorial decision
flags.note: Style guide section 12. The record is a named call, by a named scholar, for support of armed uprisings against three named sitting governments, delivered in June 2011. Publishing it in English is a political act in a way that publishing a fatwa on ablution is not, and in some jurisdictions it carries legal exposure for the publisher and conceivably for the Sheikh. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened; whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, and the fifteen years since the sermon are part of what they will have to weigh.

flags.context: في خطبته للجمعة أمس بجامع أسامة بعرفات
options: the Usamah Mosque in Arafat, the district of Nouakchott
the Usamah Mosque at Arafat near Mecca
flags.note: Arafat (عرفات) is both a moughataa of Nouakchott and the plain outside Mecca, and the Arabic is bare. The date decides it: this was a Friday in late June 2011, five months before that year's hajj, so the Nouakchott district is meant. 'Arafat' is left unqualified in the body, as the Arabic leaves it, and the identification is recorded here rather than inserted into the text. Compare record 769 in this same slice, where عرفات does mean the plain near Mecca.

flags.arabic: والذي نفسي بيده لتأمُرُنَّ بالمعروف ... / لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر ولتأخذن على يد الظالم ولتأطُرُنّه على الحق أطرا
flags.context: two prophetic reports cited in the sermon
options: translate and attribute exactly as given, with no collection and no grading
flags.note: Style guide section 4. The Sheikh names no collection and gives no grading for either report, so the English supplies neither. Both are well known and both could be sourced in a moment, but doing so would put a grading in his mouth that he did not give. A reviewing scholar may wish to add the references in an editorial apparatus kept visibly separate from his words.

flags.arabic: محاضرة قيمة حوت مواعظ بليغة، ندعوكم لمتابعتها. اضغط هنا للمتابعة.
flags.context: the final sentence of the record
options: treat as the site's own promotional furniture and omit from body_en
treat as part of the report
flags.note: The site's own endorsement of the sermon and its link to the recording, at /index.php/dawa/khotab-jomoa.html?view=media&id=1456. It is not reportage and not the Sheikh's words. Preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en. The sermon itself exists as audio; this record is a news desk's summary of it.

translator_notes: This is a news report written by the site's news desk, not a text by the Sheikh. Everything attributed to him arrives at second hand and in summary, even where the report uses quotation marks. The site must render it as reportage.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the event took place or when the report was written.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The most editorially exposed record in this slice by a wide margin. Two separate editorial_review flags, either of which is on its own sufficient to hold the record back from publication pending a decision.
The report's bullet marks are the source's own structure and are preserved.

'ثورة' is rendered 'revolution' and 'حراك' 'ferment'. Neither is softened to 'protest movement', and neither is strengthened to 'armed struggle': the Arabic words are the ones in use in 2011 and the English should carry the same weight and no more.

'من واجب الأمة' is a ruling on a collective act and is rendered by the fixed mapping of style guide section 3 as a duty. The Arabic is وَاجِب in its ordinary legal sense here, not the creedal modality of section 8.
'ولا يرعون في مسلم إلاَّ ولا ذمة' echoes Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:8 and 9:10 without quoting them. The Sheikh does not present it as a quotation, so the English does not mark it as one.
